---
title: Flexibility and thermo
---

The LS set is the dynamical model. A bond with an LS is rigid, and a bond without one may
be a rotor. The same LS decide the symmetry number, so conformer sampling, scans and the
partition function all agree.

## What the routines read now

The charge, the spin and the neighbours are fields and functions today:

```python
>>> import protomol as pm
>>> ch3 = pm.MolGraph(symbols=["C", "H", "H", "H"], bonds=[(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3)])
>>> ch3.charge, ch3.spin
(0, 1)
>>> pm.neighbors(ch3, 0)
(1, 2, 3)
>>> pm.display(ch3)  # doctest: +SKIP

```

## Conformer sampling

::: {.callout-note}
Planned: Phase 4 (`rotatable_bonds`, `rings`, `reacting_core`). Ring puckering and which
torsions in a TS core are rotors are pm open question 4.
:::

```python
torsions = pm.rotatable_bonds(smg)       # bonds to sample; never one with a bond LS
frozen = pm.reacting_core(ts)            # TS only: atoms CREST constrains
conformers = run_crest(pm.embed(smg), constrain=frozen)        # ae, illustrative
```

A conformer search can invert a centre or flip a bond, so each conformer is checked
against the graph, and kept only if nothing disagrees. Here an embedding of the graph and
of its mirror image stand in for CREST's conformers:

```python
>>> smg = pm.examples.species()
>>> conformers = [pm.embed(smg), pm.embed(pm.enantiomer(smg))]  # stand in for CREST's
>>> kept = [geo for geo in conformers if not pm.geometry_mismatches(smg, geo)]
>>> len(kept)
1

```

## Scans for the partition function

::: {.callout-note}
Planned: Phase 4 (`rotors`, `umbrellas`, `rings`, `rigid_groups`, `symmetry_number`).
:::

```python
for rotor in pm.rotors(smg):             # Rotor(axis, top, symmetry)
    scan_torsion(geo, axis=rotor.axis, moving=rotor.top, period=rotor.symmetry)  # illustrative
for umb in pm.umbrellas(smg):            # Umbrella(center, neighbors): pyramidal N, CH3
    scan_umbrella(geo, umb.center, umb.neighbors)                # illustrative
pm.rings(smg)                            # rigid in v1; ring conformers are CREST minima
pm.symmetry_number(smg)                  # total |Aut|: 12 for CH4, 18 for ethane
```

MESS-PF also takes `smg.spin` (as 2S + 1) and the symmetry number.

## The kinetics network

::: {.callout-note}
The network API is open (am Phase 6).
:::

```python
# Nodes are the identities of each TS's sides; enantiomeric nodes are lumped (illustrative)
nodes = {identity(side) for ts in channels for side in (pm.reactants(ts), pm.products(ts))}
```

Two nodes are an enantiomeric pair, to lump and adjust sigma_eff, when one's mirror image
has the other's canonical JSON:

```python
>>> smg_a = pm.examples.species()
>>> smg_b = pm.from_smiles(r"C[C@H](O)/C=C/C")
>>> pm.canonical_json(pm.enantiomer(smg_a)) == pm.canonical_json(smg_b)
True

```
